name: 16x2 LCD (no I2C, 16 pins)
desc: Shows 2 lines of 16 characters with a backlight. This plain version needs 6 data wires plus a 10kΩ knob for contrast.
variantNote: Plain 16-pin version: more wires, needs a 10kΩ potentiometer for contrast.

warn.3.3: Standard 16x2 LCDs need 5V power. 3.3V signals usually work in write-only mode (RW tied to GND), but contrast can be weak.

name: 16x2 LCD with I2C backpack
desc: The same 16x2 screen with a small adapter soldered on the back, so it needs only 4 wires. Turn the blue screw to adjust contrast.
variantNote: I2C version: only 4 wires (VCC, GND, SDA, SCL). Address is usually 0x27 or 0x3F.

warn.3.3: The I2C LCD needs 5V, and its backpack pulls SDA/SCL up to 5V. With a 3.3V board, use a level shifter on SDA and SCL.

name: 20x4 LCD with I2C backpack
desc: A bigger text screen: 4 lines of 20 characters, still only 4 wires thanks to the I2C adapter.

warn.3.3: The I2C LCD needs 5V, and its backpack pulls SDA/SCL up to 5V. With a 3.3V board, use a level shifter on SDA and SCL.

variantNote: I2C version: only 4 wires. Address usually 0x27 or 0x3F.

name: 0.96" OLED 128x64 (SSD1306, I2C)
desc: A tiny, super-sharp screen that can draw text, shapes, animations and mini games. Only 4 wires.
note: Check the pin labels! Some boards are GND-VCC-SCL-SDA and others VCC-GND-SCL-SDA. Swapping power can kill it.

name: 0.91" OLED 128x32 (SSD1306, I2C)
desc: A slim strip-shaped OLED, great for a single line of big text or a status bar.
variantNote: SSD1306 chip, but only 32 pixels tall: code must use height 32.

name: 1.3" OLED 128x64 (SH1106, I2C)
desc: A bigger OLED that is easier to read. It uses a different chip (SH1106) than the 0.96" one, so it needs a different library.
variantNote: SH1106 chip: SSD1306 code shows garbage on it. Use the U8g2 library.
note: Check the pin labels: VCC and GND positions differ between sellers.

name: TM1637 4-Digit 7-Segment Display
desc: A bright 4-digit number display with a colon in the middle, perfect for clocks, timers and scoreboards. Only 2 data wires.

name: MAX7219 8x8 LED Matrix
desc: An 8x8 grid of red LEDs for pixel art, scrolling text and tiny games. Several modules can be chained into a long sign.

warn.3.3: The MAX7219 runs on 5V and officially wants 3.5V+ signals. 3.3V boards often work, but a level shifter makes it reliable.

name: 1.8" Color TFT 128x160 (ST7735, SPI)
desc: A small full-color screen for pictures, graphs and games. It talks over SPI, which is fast but uses 5–6 wires.

warn.5: The ST7735 signal pins are 3.3V. With a 5V Arduino, use a level shifter (many people add 1kΩ resistors in series instead, but that is a hack).

name: Single 7-Segment Digit (common cathode)
desc: One big digit made of 7 LED bars plus a dot. Great for dice and counters. Each segment needs its own resistor.
note: Common cathode: the shared pin goes to GND and a HIGH pin lights a segment. Use a 220Ω resistor on each segment.

name: 2.4" Color TFT Touch 240x320 (ILI9341)
desc: A big color touchscreen for menus, games and photos. Fast SPI connection.

warn.5: Its signal pins are 3.3V. With a 5V Arduino, use a level shifter (many people add 1kΩ series resistors instead, but that's a hack).

name: 3.5" Color TFT 320x480 (ILI9488)
desc: An even bigger color screen. Best with ESP32 or Pico, which are fast enough to fill it.

warn.5: Its signal pins are 3.3V. With a 5V Arduino, use a level shifter (many people add 1kΩ series resistors instead, but that's a hack).

name: 1.3" IPS TFT 240x240 (ST7789)
desc: A small, super-sharp square color screen with wide viewing angles.

warn.5: Its signal pins are 3.3V. With a 5V Arduino, use a level shifter (many people add 1kΩ series resistors instead, but that's a hack).

name: 1.44" Color TFT 128x128 (ST7735)
desc: A tiny square color screen, great for icons, mini games and gauges.

warn.5: Its signal pins are 3.3V. With a 5V Arduino, use a level shifter (many people add 1kΩ series resistors instead, but that's a hack).

name: 1.28" Round TFT 240x240 (GC9A01)
desc: A round color screen: perfect for animated anime eyes, watch faces and gauges.

warn.5: Its signal pins are 3.3V. With a 5V Arduino, use a level shifter (many people add 1kΩ series resistors instead, but that's a hack).

name: 1.5" Color OLED 128x128 (SSD1351)
desc: A vivid color OLED with deep blacks and bright colors.

warn.5: Its signal pins are 3.3V. With a 5V Arduino, use a level shifter (many people add 1kΩ series resistors instead, but that's a hack).

name: 2.13" E-Paper Display
desc: Paper-like screen that keeps its image with zero power. Great for name badges and to-do lists.
note: E-paper refreshes slowly (1–2 s, with flashing). That's normal.

name: Nokia 5110 LCD 84x48 (PCD8544)
desc: The retro phone screen: monochrome graphics with a backlight. Cheap and nostalgic.

warn.5: The Nokia 5110 is a 3.3V display. Power it from 3.3V and use a level shifter (or series resistors) on its signal pins with 5V boards.

name: MAX7219 4-in-1 LED Matrix (32x8)
desc: Four 8x8 matrices chained into a long sign for scrolling text, clocks and pixel animations.
power: 32x8 LEDs at full brightness can draw ~1A. Keep the intensity moderate on USB power.

warn.3.3: The MAX7219 runs on 5V and officially wants 3.5V+ signals. 3.3V boards often work, but a level shifter makes it reliable.

name: MAX7219 8-Digit 7-Segment Module
desc: Eight bright digits on one board: counters, clocks and scoreboards with 3 wires.

warn.3.3: The MAX7219 runs on 5V and officially wants 3.5V+ signals. A level shifter makes it reliable with 3.3V boards.

name: 4-Digit 7-Segment Display (bare, common cathode)
desc: Four digits without a driver chip: you light them one at a time very fast ("multiplexing").
note: Needs 12 pins and 8 resistors (220Ω). The TM1637 module is far easier for beginners.

name: 128x64 Graphic LCD (ST7920)
desc: A big blue graphic LCD that can show text and drawings, used in many 3D printers.

name: 0.96" OLED 128x64 (SSD1306, SPI 7-pin)
desc: The same little OLED as the I2C version, but connected over faster SPI with 7 pins.
variantNote: SPI version: 7 pins (GND, VCC, D0/SCK, D1/MOSI, RES, DC, CS). Different wiring and code than I2C.

warn.5: Its signal pins connect straight to the 3.3V chip. Many people use it directly with 5V boards, but a level shifter is safer.

name: 10-Segment LED Bar Graph
desc: Ten LEDs in one block, for level meters and battery gauges. Each segment needs its own resistor.
note: One 220Ω resistor per segment (or use a 74HC595 to save pins).

name: 20x4 LCD (no I2C, 16 pins)
desc: A 4-line, 20-character text LCD without the I2C backpack: more wires, same screen.
variantNote: Plain 16-pin version: 6 data wires plus a 10kΩ contrast potentiometer.

name: LCD Keypad Shield (16x2 + 5 buttons)
desc: A shield that plugs straight onto an Uno: a 16x2 LCD plus 5 buttons, no wiring needed.
note: Buttons share one analog pin (A0). Some clones have a backlight transistor fault: don't set pin 10 to OUTPUT HIGH.
